You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — General Cable / Prysmian realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (~2021-2023)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the acquired company deregistered shortly
> after closing and its acquirer does not file U.S. periodic reports, no audited public
> financial record exists for the fixed ~2021-2023 outcome window; this sub-dossier
> states that plainly rather than inferring an outcome. It contains no information about
> how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On June 18, 2018, General Cable Corporation filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination
  of registration (Rule 12g-4(a)(1), Rule 12h-3(b)(1)(i)) of its common stock, 5.750%
  Senior Notes due 2022, and Subordinated Convertible Notes due 2029, recording a single
  holder of record of the common stock. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-194946, Form 15-12B]
- EDGAR's filing history for General Cable (CIK 0000886035) shows no Form 10-K, 10-Q, or
  other periodic report after the May 7, 2018 Form 10-Q; the only post-closing entries
  are transaction-related filings and a single third-party Schedule 13G/A dated
  2019-02-14. No audited public financial statements exist for this registrant covering
  the ~2021-2023 outcome window. [SRC: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000886035.json]
- Prysmian S.p.A. holds an SEC filer identifier (CIK 0001437672), but every filing under
  it is a Form F-6EF/F-6 POS registering or amending an American Depositary Receipt
  facility for its ordinary shares; no Form 10-K, 20-F, or other annual/periodic
  operating report has been filed under that CIK, and its ordinary shares trade on the
  Borsa Italiana rather than a U.S. exchange. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001437672&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=100&output=atom]

## Realized record traceable through press disclosures (non-financial; no primary financial scalar available)
- On December 21, 2021, Prysmian Group announced the legal-entity merger of General Cable
  Industries, Inc. and Prysmian Cables and Systems USA, LLC, with the resulting U.S.
  operations adopting the name "Prysmian Group US" effective January 1, 2022, describing
  this as concluding the integration process begun with the 2018 acquisition. [SRC: https://na.prysmian.com/resources/press-releases/prysmian-group-announces-legal-entity-integration-and-finalizes-rebranding-with-general-cable-in-the-united-states]
- At that announcement, the combined North American operation was described as comprising
  27 manufacturing facilities, 8 distribution centers, 6 R&D centers, and over 5,800
  employees, with stated planned investments of $100 million (U.S. Power Distribution
  plants) and $85 million (Telecom plant equipment/technology). [SRC: https://na.prysmian.com/resources/press-releases/prysmian-group-announces-legal-entity-integration-and-finalizes-rebranding-with-general-cable-in-the-united-states]
- Prysmian Group's CEO was quoted: "Three years after joining forces, we are stronger
  than ever ... we offer the most complete portfolio of wire and cable solutions crucial
  to supporting the energy transition and digital transformation in the U.S." These press
  disclosures describe organizational/branding integration milestones and do not report
  a segment- or entity-level financial scalar attributable specifically to the formerly
  separate General Cable business. [SRC: https://na.prysmian.com/resources/press-releases/prysmian-group-announces-legal-entity-integration-and-finalizes-rebranding-with-general-cable-in-the-united-states]

## Items noted but not verifiable within this dossier
- No divestiture, bankruptcy, dissolution, or impairment/write-down disclosure specific
  to the acquired General Cable business was located in the ~2021-2023 window; this
  absence reflects the absence of a located public record, not itself an outcome finding.
  [UNVERIFIED]
- No separately reported financial performance scalar (net income/loss, revenue,
  goodwill impairment) for the acquired business, isolated from Prysmian's consolidated
  results, was located for the outcome window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- General Cable deregistered its securities within two weeks of closing (Form 15-12B,
  June 18, 2018), and its acquirer, Prysmian S.p.A., does not file U.S. annual or
  periodic operating reports (its SEC CIK covers only an ADR facility); no primary-filing
  financial record therefore exists for the acquired business at the fixed ~2021-2023
  outcome window. The only located public record within the window is a December 2021
  Prysmian press release describing a legal-entity merger and rebranding of the former
  General Cable U.S. operations to "Prysmian Group US," effective January 1, 2022,
  alongside stated facility counts, headcount, and planned capital investment. This case
  is accordingly coded uncertain on the outcome for lack of a public financial record,
  per the no-record convention. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-194946, Form 15-12B] [SRC: https://na.prysmian.com/resources/press-releases/prysmian-group-announces-legal-entity-integration-and-finalizes-rebranding-with-general-cable-in-the-united-states]

[SLICE END]
